text: DEQ, in consultation with the Virginia Department of Health and Virginia Energy, shall conduct or oversee a cumulative-impact review of diesel and other backup-generation operations associated with data centers. The review shall consider: the number, capacity, fuel type, expected operating hours, and geographic concentration of backup generators; cumulative emissions and localized air-quality impacts, particularly in communities hosting multiple data-center facilities; available measures to reduce emissions, protect public health, and improve transparency; and measures to promote retrofit of Tier II gen-sets to Tier IV or equivalent emissions controls, battery storage, fuel cells, clean firm generation, non-diesel alternatives, and other feasible technologies that can meet reliability needs while reducing public-health and environmental impacts from backup generation.

source.citation: Virginia Executive Order 22 (2026), Establishing New Nation-Leading Standards and Initiatives to Implement the Virginia Data Center Accountability Framework and Responding to Unprecedented Risk from Artificial Intelligence, signed September 18 2026

notes: Findings due on or about March 17 2027. First cumulative-impact review of backup generation identified in this corpus. Relevant to the growing use of on-site generation to serve load prior to interconnection.
confidence_note: Directs a review. Imposes no obligation on any operator. Sets no emissions limit and no operating-hour limit. The order does not anywhere distinguish standby generation from continuous-duty on-site generation, and this entry does not establish that the review reaches primary generation.
